t: Eight dishes on the testis kitchen counter
story: Picture a busy **kitchen** and a counter of tagged dishes. A tray of neat **fried eggs** sits under cloth strips crowded with buzzing flies: the seminoma. A **no-AFP sign** hangs over it, because a pure seminoma never makes AFP. Beside it is a bloody, burnt bowl of raw **batter**: embryonal carcinoma. A toddler in a **high chair** wears a bib stamped AFP: the yolk sac tumor of small boys. A **rocket** stamped hCG streaks straight to the lungs: choriocarcinoma. A **three-layer cake** with hair, tooth and bone is the teratoma. A **golden-brown nugget** with tiny rods is the Leydig cell tumor. A **bathroom scale** weighing the whole counter reads LDH.
keys: Seminoma: fried-egg cells with clear cytoplasm and fibrous septa full of lymphocytes. Very radiosensitive, spreads late, excellent prognosis.
Pure seminoma never makes AFP, so a raised AFP means a nonseminomatous part. Mildly raised hCG still fits seminoma.
Embryonal carcinoma: a hemorrhagic, necrotic mass of primitive cells that can be painful and may raise AFP or hCG.
Yolk sac tumor: the most common testicular tumor in boys under 3. It secretes AFP and shows Schiller-Duval bodies.
Choriocarcinoma: very high hCG and early blood spread to the lungs. The hCG can cause gynecomastia and hyperthyroidism.
Teratoma has tissue from all three germ layers, and in adult men even mature-looking teratoma can metastasize.
Leydig cell tumor: golden-brown nodule with rod-shaped Reinke crystals. Androgens cause precocious puberty in boys; converted estrogen causes gynecomastia in men.
LDH tracks tumor bulk, so it helps with prognosis, not with typing the tumor.
